questions.q: Which of the following describes a census?
a: Collecting data from every member of a population
Collecting data from a small representative subgroup
Collecting data only from volunteers
Collecting data from a random sample

questions.q: What is a major advantage of taking a sample instead of conducting a census?
a: It is always 100 percent accurate
It is quicker, cheaper, and less disruptive
It avoids all forms of bias
It includes every single individual

questions.q: What type of data is collected when people are asked to name their favorite color?
a: Continuous numerical data
Discrete numerical data
Categorical (qualitative) data
Ordinal data

questions.q: Which of the following represents discrete numerical data?
a: Height of students in meters
Time taken to run a race
Temperature throughout the day
Number of pets in a household

questions.q: A researcher stands outside a specific supermarket and asks every tenth customer leaving about their shopping habits. What sampling method is this?
a: Systematic sampling
Random sampling
Quota sampling
Stratified sampling

questions.q: Why might a survey conducted by a fast-food company claiming '90 percent of people love our burgers' be biased?
a: The sample size was too large
The funding source may influence the wording or audience of the survey
It was a complete census
It used random numbers

questions.q: Which of the following questions is considered leading and therefore poorly worded?
a: How many times do you eat fruit each week?
What is your opinion on school lunches?
Don't you agree that mathematics is the most important subject?
How long is your journey to school?

questions.q: What is a pilot survey used for?
a: To collect the final published data
To train airplane pilots in statistics
To replace a full census entirely
To test the questionnaire design and identify any problems before the main survey

questions.q: In a school of 800 pupils, a researcher wants a stratified sample of 80 pupils. If Year 8 has 200 pupils, how many students from Year 8 should be in the sample?
Which of the following data types is continuous?
a: Number of cars in a parking lot
Mass of parcels in kilograms
Shoe size in UK numbers
Number of goals scored in a match

questions.q: What is random sampling designed to ensure?
a: That the survey takes as little time as possible
That only people with strong opinions are heard
Every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected
That every subgroup is represented proportionally

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of postal questionnaires?
a: They are too expensive to print
The interviewer influences the answers directly
They take place only in laboratories
They typically suffer from a very low response rate

questions.q: A questionnaire asks: 'How many hours of television do you watch? A) 0-2 hours B) 2-4 hours C) 4-6 hours'. What is the main flaw with these response options?
a: The categories overlap for someone who watches exactly 2 or 4 hours
There are too many options
The options are not numerical
The question is leading

questions.q: What does 'population' mean in statistics?
a: The total number of people living in a country
The entire group of individuals or items that you want to study
The sample group chosen for an interview
The group of people who refuse to answer

questions.q: When is a census preferred over a sample?
a: When testing the lifespan of lightbulbs (destructive testing)
When the population is extremely large and infinite
When 100 percent accuracy and complete data are required for a small population
When there is very little time and budget

questions.q: Which sampling method involves dividing the population into subgroups and taking random samples from each proportional to their size?
a: Random sampling
Opportunity sampling
Cluster sampling
Stratified sampling

questions.q: What is opportunity (convenience) sampling?
a: Choosing members of the population who are easiest and most readily available to access
Selecting every fifth person from a complete register
Using a computer random number generator
Interviewing people chosen by a government official

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of primary data?
a: Data downloaded from a government census website
Data collected by yourself through a direct survey or experiment
Data read from a textbook table
Data found in a historical archive

questions.q: What is secondary data?
a: Data collected by an assistant rather than the main researcher
Data that has been proven false
Data collected by someone else that you use for your own research
Data that is numerical rather than categorical

questions.q: Which question is clear, neutral, and well-designed for a survey about exercise?
a: Why do you hate exercising?
How can you be so lazy as to not exercise?
Don't you agree that everyone should run daily?
How many days a week do you engage in physical activity?

questions.q: What is non-response bias?
a: Bias that occurs when people who do not respond to a survey have different views from those who do
Bias caused by asking leading questions
Bias caused by broken measuring equipment
Bias resulting from a sample size that is too large

questions.q: If a researcher interviews only their friends to find out the most popular hobby in the whole city, what kind of sampling bias is present?
a: Stratified bias
Sampling bias / Opportunity bias
Random error
Census error

questions.q: Which of the following represents ordinal categorical data?
a: Eye color (Blue, Brown, Green)
Types of pets (Cat, Dog, Fish)
Customer satisfaction rating (Poor, Satisfactory, Excellent)
Shoe brand (Nike, Adidas, Puma)

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of data cleaning before analysis?
a: To change the results to match what you want
To make the data file smaller in size
To remove all numerical values
To identify and correct errors, anomalies, or missing values

questions.q: When designing a tally chart for grouped continuous data (e.g., heights), how should the classes be structured?
a: Non-overlapping and continuous (e.g., 10 to less than 20, 20 to less than 30)
Randomly assigned ranges
Single exact integer values only

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of a good statistical hypothesis?
a: It is always proven true
It is testable based on collected data
It contains no numbers
It is based entirely on personal opinion

questions.q: What does a high response rate in a survey indicate?
a: The survey questions were too difficult
The sample size was too small
The findings are likely to be more reliable and representative of the population
The survey was conducted online

questions.q: Which data collection tool is best suited for recording the frequency of different types of cars passing a school gate?
a: A formal interview
An online questionnaire
A postal survey
A tally chart / observation sheet

questions.q: What is an outlier in a dataset?
a: A data value that is significantly higher or lower than most other values
The exact middle value of a dataset
The most frequently occurring value
The average value of the dataset

questions.q: Why is random number generation often used in selecting a sample?
a: To ensure the researcher knows every participant personally
To eliminate human selection bias
To guarantee that all respondents give the same answer
To reduce the cost of printing questionnaires

questions.q: Which of the following best describes qualitative data?
a: Data that can be measured with numbers and decimals
Data representing counts or quantities
Data describing qualities, characteristics, or categories
Data collected exclusively from thermometers

questions.q: What is a structured interview?
a: An informal chat with no fixed questions
An interview where the questions change completely for every person
An interview conducted via email
An interview where the researcher asks a standard set of predetermined questions in the same order

questions.q: What is the term for a small-scale trial of a survey used to check for ambiguities in questions?
a: Pilot study
Control group trial
Census test
Stratified audit

questions.q: Which factor is most critical when determining the required sample size for a large population?
a: The budget and desired level of precision / confidence
The favorite color of the researcher
The time of day the survey is printed
The number of pages in the questionnaire

questions.q: What is a closed question in a questionnaire?
a: A question that allows respondents to write any paragraph answer they want
A question that is too difficult to understand
A question that provides a limited set of fixed response options
A question at the very end of a survey

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of online surveys?
a: They are too expensive to distribute
They take weeks to reach respondents
They cannot include multiple-choice questions
They may exclude people without internet access or digital literacy

questions.q: What is an open question?
a: A question where respondents can write their own answers in their own words without pre-set options
A question with 'Yes' or 'No' only
A multiple-choice question
A question about outdoor activities

questions.q: What is the main purpose of grouping raw numerical data into class intervals?
a: To make the data completely inaccurate
To simplify and summarize large amounts of data to make patterns clearer
To increase the number of outliers
To hide missing values

questions.q: Which term describes a sample that does not accurately reflect the wider population?
a: A census sample
A random sample
A biased sample
A stratified sample

questions.q: What is the primary ethical consideration when conducting a survey involving human participants?
a: Ensuring all participants are paid money
Making sure the survey takes less than one minute
Guaranteeing that questions are multiple-choice
Obtaining informed consent and maintaining participant confidentiality
